title: Helmand Valley Authority irrigation project launched
note: Morrison-Knudsen contracted from 1946; HAVA formally established 1952. Year given (1950) is approximate start of major work — accurate in spirit, project began mid-1940s.

title: Pashtunistan dispute escalates with Pakistan
note: Afghanistan was the sole UN member to vote against Pakistan's admission. Well-documented historical fact.

title: Afghanistan-Pakistan border tensions cause trade disruption
note: Pashtunistan dispute and Pakistan trade/transit restrictions on landlocked Afghanistan are well documented throughout early 1950s.

title: Soviet Union extends trade and transit agreements to Afghanistan
note: Soviet economic engagement began in earnest in early 1950s as Pakistan closed transit routes; trade agreements confirmed by multiple Cold War histories.

title: Liberal newspapers suppressed by Afghan government
note: The liberal parliament 1949-1952 ended with press suppression. The event is dated to 1952 but the crackdown is more precisely associated with Daoud's arrival in 1953 — slight year ambiguity but the phenomenon is real.

title: Afghanistan requests US military aid but is refused
note: US refusal of Afghan military aid requests in early 1950s is documented in Cold War histories; drove Afghanistan toward Soviet arms.

title: Prince Mohammed Daoud Khan becomes Prime Minister
note: Appointed September 1953 by King Zahir Shah. Confirmed by multiple sources.

title: Afghanistan renews Pashtunistan demands against Pakistan
note: Daoud's intensification of Pashtunistan claims is a central feature of his 1953-1963 tenure, well-documented.

title: Afghanistan accepts Soviet economic and technical assistance
note: Soviet technical cooperation agreements beginning 1954-1955 confirmed. Preceded the large 1955 $100M loan.

title: Afghanistan rejects US proposal to join anti-Soviet pact
note: Afghanistan's non-alignment and refusal to join Baghdad Pact is well-documented Cold War policy under Daoud.

title: Afghanistan-Pakistan diplomatic crisis and border closure
note: 1955 crisis including attack on Pakistani diplomatic missions in Kabul and brief severance of relations is well-documented.

title: Soviet leaders Khrushchev and Bulganin visit Kabul pledging $100 million loan
note: December 1955 visit confirmed by Wilson Center archives. $100M credit pledge confirmed.

title: Soviet Union begins construction of Salang Highway tunnel
note: Agreement signed 1955, construction began 1956, completed 1964. Confirmed.

title: Afghanistan accepts Soviet military equipment and training
note: Soviet military equipment and training agreements from mid-1950s are well-documented in Afghan Cold War history.

title: Kabul-Kandahar highway completed with US funding
note: The paved Kabul-Kandahar highway was completed in 1966 by US Army Corps of Engineers/USAID, not 1957. A gravel road existed earlier but the modern paved highway completion date is wrong by nearly a decade.

title: Afghan government launches first five-year development plan
note: Afghanistan's First Five-Year Economic and Social Development Plan (1956-1961) under Daoud is confirmed in multiple sources.

title: Daoud government introduces voluntary unveiling for women
note: August 1959 Jeshyn festival unveiling by Queen Humaira and PM wife confirmed by Wikipedia and multiple sources. Daoud's voluntary approach confirmed.

title: Afghanistan-Pakistan Pashtunistan crisis reignites with border clashes
note: Border tensions and clashes in 1960 documented as part of ongoing Pashtunistan crisis.

title: Afghanistan and Pakistan sever diplomatic relations
note: Diplomatic severance and border closure in 1961 is well-documented; lasted until 1963.

title: Afghan economy strained by Pakistan border closure
note: Economic damage from Pakistan border closure contributing to Daoud's eventual resignation is confirmed.

title: Afghan-Pakistani trade embargo causes severe economic hardship
note: Two-year border closure and economic hardship from 1961-1963 is well-documented.

title: Prime Minister Daoud Khan forced to resign by King Zahir Shah
note: Daoud resigned/was dismissed March 1963 due to economic damage from Pakistan policy. Confirmed.

title: Afghanistan and Pakistan restore diplomatic relations
note: Border reopened May 1963 after Daoud's resignation. Confirmed.

title: New Afghan constitution promulgated establishing constitutional monarchy
note: 1964 constitution establishing constitutional monarchy with bicameral parliament confirmed.

title: Salang Highway tunnel through Hindu Kush completed
note: Tunnel opened 1964 confirmed by Wikipedia and multiple engineering sources.

title: Women gain voting rights and first contested parliamentary elections held
note: 1964 constitution granted universal suffrage. First competitive elections held in 1965 (not 1964); the constitution was 1964 but elections were held in 1965. Minor year ambiguity but core claims accurate.

title: Founding of Peoples Democratic Party of Afghanistan (PDPA)
note: PDPA was founded January 1, 1965, not 1964. The year is wrong by one year. This is a common confabulation error.

title: PDPA splits into Khalq and Parcham factions
note: Split into Khalq and Parcham is documented; the formal break was 1967 but factional tensions visible from 1965 founding. Event is essentially accurate.

title: Student protests erupt in Kabul over political restrictions
note: October 25, 1965 student protests in Kabul confirmed; police fired on demonstrators.

title: Islamist student movement emerges at Kabul University
note: Islamist movement at Kabul University in mid-1960s with Rabbani, Hekmatyar is confirmed in multiple historical sources.

title: Natural gas exports to Soviet Union begin from northern Afghanistan
note: Gas exports began 1967 via Sheberghan-Keleft pipeline. Confirmed.

title: Devastating drought causes famine conditions in rural Afghanistan
note: Late 1960s drought affecting Afghanistan documented; led into the 1971-72 famine.

title: Severe famine strikes central Afghanistan killing thousands
note: 1971-72 famine confirmed; estimates of deaths vary (some sources say 100,000+). The 80,000-100,000 figure is within range of cited estimates.

title: Daoud Khan overthrows monarchy in bloodless coup
note: July 17 1973 coup by Daoud while Zahir Shah was in Italy. Confirmed.

title: Republic of Afghanistan declared under President Daoud
note: Daoud declared republic, dissolved parliament, named himself president and PM. Confirmed.

title: Pakistan hosts Afghan Islamist militants in response to Pashtunistan
note: Pakistan's ISI support for Afghan Islamist exiles starting 1973 is confirmed as origin of mujahideen patronage.

title: Afghan Islamist uprising attempt in Panjshir Valley fails
note: The Panjshir uprising led by Massoud happened in 1975, not 1974. Year is wrong. The event occurred July 1975.

title: Islamist insurgency attempt suppressed across eastern provinces
note: 1975 coordinated Islamist uprisings in multiple provinces (Panjshir, Kunar, Laghman) confirmed; failure drove groups to Pakistan.

title: Daoud distances Afghanistan from Soviet Union toward Iran and Gulf
note: Daoud's pivot away from USSR toward Iran and Arab states in mid-1970s is well-documented.

title: PDPA Khalq and Parcham factions reconcile under Soviet pressure
note: Soviet-pressured reunification in 1977 (formal agreement March 1977) — event placed at 1976 is slightly early; formal unity was 1977. Minor year ambiguity.

title: Daoud meets Soviet leader Brezhnev amid rising tensions
note: April 1977 Moscow visit confirmed; Brezhnev complained about NATO experts; Daoud responded defiantly. Confirmed acrimonious.

title: Afghan government arrests PDPA leaders
note: PDPA leaders were arrested in April 1978 (just before the Saur Revolution), not 1977. The event description fits the April 25-26, 1978 arrests that triggered the coup. Year is wrong by one year.

title: Saur Revolution: PDPA military coup overthrows and kills Daoud
note: April 27-28 1978 coup killing Daoud and family confirmed.

title: Democratic Republic of Afghanistan declared under Taraki
note: Taraki as President/PM of Democratic Republic confirmed.

title: PDPA launches radical land reform and bans religion in public life
note: PDPA land reform, debt cancellation, anti-Islamic measures confirmed; triggered rural resistance.

title: Parcham faction purged; Afghan-Soviet Friendship Treaty signed
note: Parcham purge and Afghan-Soviet Friendship Treaty (December 1978) confirmed.

title: Rural uprising against communist government begins in Nuristan
note: Nuristan as a key early center of anti-PDPA resistance in 1978 is documented.

title: Mass arrests and executions of political opponents by PDPA
note: PDPA mass repression of opponents confirmed by HRW and multiple sources.

title: Herat uprising against communist government killed thousands
note: March 1979 Herat uprising confirmed; ~50 Soviet advisers killed; 3,000-25,000 civilians killed in government crackdown. Event says 'dozens of Soviet advisers' — actual figure was approximately 50.

title: Hafizullah Amin murders President Taraki in palace coup
note: Taraki strangled/smothered on Amin's orders in October 1979. Soviet outrage confirmed.

title: CIA begins covert arms supply to Afghan mujahideen
note: Carter authorized first covert aid July 3, 1979; arms supply expanded after December invasion. Confirmed.

title: Soviet Union invades Afghanistan with 80,000 troops
note: December 24-27 1979 invasion confirmed. Initial force ~30,000 rising to 100,000 within weeks; '80,000' figure is within commonly cited range.

title: Babrak Karmal installed as Afghan leader by Soviets
note: Karmal flown in from exile to replace Amin. Confirmed.

title: UN General Assembly demands Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan
note: UNGA Resolution ES-6/2 passed 104-18 demanding Soviet withdrawal. Confirmed.

title: United States imposes grain embargo and boycotts Moscow Olympics
note: Carter grain embargo and 1980 Moscow Olympics boycott in response to Afghanistan invasion confirmed.

title: Mujahideen resistance coalitions form in Pakistan and Iran
note: Pakistan-based Seven Party Alliance and Iran-based Shia coalitions documented in Cold War histories.

title: Soviet scorched-earth tactics devastate Afghan agriculture and drive refugee crisis
note: Soviet scorched-earth tactics and refugee crisis of 1980 (1M+ in Pakistan by end of 1980) documented.

title: Operation Cyclone CIA covert program formally expanded
note: Carter administration expanded Operation Cyclone after Soviet invasion; Reagan further expanded it. Confirmed.

title: Reagan administration dramatically increases mujahideen funding
note: Reagan escalation of Operation Cyclone confirmed; Saudi matching of US contributions confirmed.

title: Ahmad Shah Massoud repels Soviet offensives in Panjshir
note: Multiple Soviet offensives into Panjshir repelled by Massoud; 1981 saw 4th offensive. Confirmed.

title: International Islamic volunteer fighters begin arriving in Afghanistan
note: Arab volunteers including bin Laden documented arriving from early 1980s. Category 'terrorist_attack' is inappropriate for this event (it describes a migration/foreign fighter phenomenon), but the factual claim is accurate.

title: Afghan refugee population exceeds 3 million in Pakistan alone
note: 3M+ Afghan refugees in Pakistan by 1982 confirmed by UNHCR records.

title: UN-mediated Geneva Talks on Afghanistan begin
note: UN mediator Diego Cordovez began indirect Geneva talks in 1982. Confirmed.

title: Soviet forces mount largest offensive of the war in Panjshir
note: The largest Panjshir offensive was the 7th in April 1984 (20,000+ troops), not 1983. The 1983 period saw the 6th offensive. Year may be off; could not confirm 1983 as 'largest offensive of the war.'

title: Landmine contamination becomes major civilian casualty issue
note: Landmine contamination as a major issue during Soviet-Afghan war is well-documented.

title: Mujahideen factions receive over $200 million in CIA-Saudi aid
note: CIA-Saudi aid exceeding $200M in 1984, channeled through ISI, confirmed.

title: Saudi-funded madrassas in refugee camps promote radical Islamist ideology
note: Saudi-funded madrassas in Pakistani refugee camps radicalized youth in 1980s — documented as precursor to Taliban.

title: Mikhail Gorbachev becomes Soviet General Secretary and reassesses Afghan war
note: Gorbachev assumed power March 1985; immediately began reassessing Afghan war. 'Bleeding wound' phrase used in February 1986 speech, not 1985 — minor detail inaccuracy.

title: CIA delivers Stinger surface-to-air missiles to mujahideen
note: First Stingers delivered September 1986; first downing September 25, 1986. Confirmed.

title: Babrak Karmal replaced by Mohammad Najibullah as Afghan leader
note: Najibullah replaced Karmal in 1986 as Soviet-preferred leader. Confirmed.

title: Najibullah launches National Reconciliation policy
note: National Reconciliation policy announced 1986-1987 as part of Soviet withdrawal preparations. Confirmed.

title: Gorbachev announces Soviet withdrawal plan
note: Gorbachev public withdrawal announcement February 8, 1988 (not 1987 — the 1987 statement was more informal). The formal public announcement was 1988. Slight year inaccuracy.

title: Geneva Accords signed for Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan
note: Signed April 14, 1988. Confirmed. Critique of excluding mujahideen is accurate.

title: Osama bin Laden founds Al-Qaeda in Peshawar
note: Al-Qaeda founded August 1988 in Peshawar. Zawahiri involvement is slightly overstated as co-founder at this stage — he merged his Egyptian Islamic Jihad into al-Qaeda later — but founding year and location confirmed.

title: Last Soviet troops leave Afghanistan
note: General Gromov last to cross February 15, 1989. Confirmed.

title: Mujahideen fail to capture Jalalabad in costly frontal assault
note: March 1989 Jalalabad assault failure confirmed; Pakistani-planned conventional attack repulsed.

title: Afghan refugee population peaks at approximately 6 million
note: Peak refugee figure of ~6M (3.5M Pakistan, 2.5M Iran) in late 1980s confirmed.

title: Failed military coup against Najibullah by Khalq faction
note: March 6, 1990 coup attempt by General Tanai confirmed; fled to Pakistan after failure.

title: Opium production expands massively during war years
note: Afghanistan's rise as top opium producer in 1980s-1990s confirmed; CIA/ISI tolerance of drug trafficking by allied commanders documented.

title: Soviet Union collapses ending USSR support for Najibullah
note: USSR dissolution December 1991 ended support for Najibullah. Confirmed.

title: Najibullah government collapses as mujahideen capture Kabul
note: April 1992 collapse with Dostum defection confirmed; Najibullah in UN compound until 1996 murder confirmed.

title: Peshawar Accords create mujahideen transitional government
note: April 1992 Peshawar Accords and Mojaddedi as transitional head confirmed.

title: Gulbuddin Hekmatyar begins rocket attacks on Kabul
note: Hekmatyar's indiscriminate rocket bombardment of Kabul from 1992 confirmed.

title: Civil war between mujahideen factions devastates Kabul
note: 1993 fighting between Rabbani-Massoud and Hekmatyar causing tens of thousands of civilian deaths confirmed.

title: Afshar massacre committed by Sayyaf and Massoud forces
note: February 11, 1993 Afshar massacre confirmed. Sayyaf's forces primarily responsible; Massoud's forces also involved.

title: Taliban movement emerges in Kandahar Province
note: Taliban formation in Kandahar 1994 under Mullah Omar confirmed.

title: Taliban captures Kandahar city from mujahideen factions
note: Taliban captured Kandahar November 1994. Confirmed.

title: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia provide covert support to Taliban
note: Pakistani ISI and Saudi support for Taliban from 1994 documented in multiple sources.

title: Taliban captures Herat Province and imposes strict Islamic law
note: Taliban capture of Herat September 1995 confirmed; immediate imposition of strict Islamic law confirmed.

title: Taliban defeats and kills Hezb-e-Wahdat leader Mazari
note: Mazari captured and killed by Taliban March 1995. Confirmed.

title: Taliban captures Kabul and establishes Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan
note: September 27, 1996 Taliban capture of Kabul confirmed; Najibullah hanged; Islamic Emirate declared.

title: Taliban bans women from work, education, and public life
note: Immediate Taliban gender restrictions upon Kabul takeover confirmed.

title: Northern Alliance formed against Taliban
note: Northern Alliance formation with Massoud, Dostum, Rabbani, Hazara commanders confirmed.

title: Osama bin Laden returns to Afghanistan under Taliban protection
note: Bin Laden expelled from Sudan, arrived in Afghanistan 1996 under Taliban protection. Confirmed.

title: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia recognize Taliban government
note: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and UAE were the only three countries to recognize Taliban government. Confirmed.

title: Al-Qaeda bombs US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania
note: August 7, 1998 bombings killed 224 people. Confirmed.

title: US launches cruise missile strikes on Afghan al-Qaeda camps
note: Operation Infinite Reach cruise missile strikes August 20, 1998 on Afghanistan and Sudan confirmed. ~70 missiles fired.

title: Taliban captures Mazar-e-Sharif and massacres Hazara civilians
note: August 1998 Mazar-i-Sharif massacre confirmed; thousands killed (HRW says 10,000+); Iranian diplomats killed. Confirmed.

title: Massive earthquakes kill thousands in northern Takhar Province
note: February 1998 earthquake (~2,300-4,000 deaths) and May 1998 earthquake (~4,000-4,500 deaths) both in Takhar/northern Afghanistan confirmed.

title: UN imposes sanctions on Taliban over al-Qaeda harboring
note: UNSC Resolution 1267 (1999) imposing sanctions on Taliban confirmed.

title: Severe multi-year drought begins devastating Afghan agriculture
note: Multi-year drought beginning late 1990s and peaking 2000-2002 documented.

title: Taliban bans poppy cultivation declaring drugs un-Islamic
note: July 2000 Mullah Omar edict; 94-99% production drop confirmed for 2001 crop.

title: Al-Qaeda attack on USS Cole kills 17 US sailors
note: October 12, 2000 USS Cole bombing killing 17 sailors confirmed. Planned from Afghanistan.

title: Taliban destroys ancient Bamiyan Buddha statues
note: March 2001 destruction confirmed. Event says '1,500-year-old' — statues were 6th century (1400-1500 years old in 2001). Accurate.

title: Ahmad Shah Massoud assassinated by al-Qaeda suicide bombers
note: September 9, 2001 assassination by al-Qaeda operatives posing as journalists confirmed.

title: September 11 attacks trigger US decision to invade Afghanistan
note: 9/11 attacks and subsequent decision to invade after Taliban refused to surrender bin Laden confirmed.

title: US-led Operation Enduring Freedom begins bombing Afghanistan
note: October 7, 2001 airstrikes confirmed.

title: Northern Alliance captures Kabul with US air support
note: Northern Alliance entered Kabul November 13, 2001. Confirmed.

title: Battle of Tora Bora: bin Laden escapes into Pakistan
note: December 2001 Tora Bora battle and bin Laden's escape to Pakistan confirmed.

title: Bonn Agreement establishes Afghan Interim Authority
note: December 5, 2001 Bonn Agreement establishing Interim Authority under Karzai confirmed.

title: Emergency Loya Jirga selects transitional government under Karzai
note: June 2002 Loya Jirga confirming Karzai confirmed.

title: International Security Assistance Force (ISAF) established in Kabul
note: ISAF authorized by UNSC January 2002, UK-led. Confirmed.

title: Afghan refugee repatriation begins with UNHCR assistance
note: ~1.8M Afghan refugees returned in 2002 confirmed by UNHCR.

title: Taliban insurgency begins reforming in Pakistani sanctuaries
note: Taliban reconstitution in Pakistan's FATA and Quetta from 2002 is well-documented.

title: Operation Anaconda targets al-Qaeda remnants in Shah-i-Kot Valley
note: March 2002 Operation Anaconda in Shah-i-Kot Valley confirmed.

title: NATO assumes command of ISAF mission in Afghanistan
note: NATO took command August 2003. Confirmed.

title: Taliban insurgency significantly intensifies in southern Afghanistan
note: Marked increase in Taliban attacks 2003-2004 documented.

title: US diverts military and intelligence resources to Iraq invasion
note: March 2003 Iraq invasion diverting resources from Afghanistan is widely documented.

title: New Afghan constitution adopted establishing Islamic Republic
note: January 2004 constitution establishing Islamic Republic confirmed.

title: Hamid Karzai elected president in first direct Afghan election
note: October 2004 election, Karzai won ~55%. Confirmed.

title: Opium poppy production surges to record levels
note: 2004 record opium production surge confirmed. UNODC 4,200 metric tons figure confirmed.

title: Taliban suicide bombing campaign begins targeting civilians
note: Taliban adoption of suicide bombing tactics from 2004 with Iraqi insurgency model influence documented.

title: Afghan parliamentary elections held for first time in decades
note: September 2005 parliamentary elections confirmed; first since 1969.

title: Insurgent attacks increase dramatically across southern Afghanistan
note: More than doubling of insurgent attacks in 2005 vs 2004 documented.

title: NATO expands to southern Afghanistan taking over from US forces
note: NATO expansion to south July 2006 with British, Canadian, Dutch forces confirmed.

title: Taliban surge in southern Afghanistan largest since 2001
note: 2006 Taliban offensive in Helmand and Kandahar confirmed as largest since 2001.

title: Surge in Taliban attacks kills thousands across Afghanistan
note: 2007 documented as bloodiest year since 2001 with 6,000+ deaths. Confirmed.

title: Afghanistan opium production reaches all-time record
note: 2007 record 8,200 metric tons / 93% world supply confirmed by UNODC.

title: US increases drone strikes in Pakistani tribal areas
note: Bush administration drone strike escalation in FATA 2008 confirmed.

title: Suicide bombing of Indian embassy in Kabul kills 58
note: July 7, 2008 bombing killing 58 confirmed; defense attache (Brigadier Mehta) killed. ISI involvement alleged.

title: Kandahar prison break frees 1,200 Taliban prisoners
note: June 13, 2008 Sarposa prison break freeing ~1,200 (including ~400-1,000 depending on source) confirmed.

title: Obama announces 30,000 troop surge to Afghanistan
note: December 1, 2009 West Point speech announcing 30,000 troop surge confirmed; 2011 withdrawal date mentioned.

title: Contested presidential election plunges Afghanistan into political crisis
note: August 2009 election fraud with ~1M fraudulent Karzai votes confirmed; Abdullah withdrew from runoff.

title: Operation Moshtarak NATO offensive in Helmand Province
note: February 13, 2010 launch of Operation Moshtarak targeting Marjah confirmed.

title: Kabul Bank scandal exposes massive financial fraud
note: 2010 Kabul Bank collapse with ~$900M fraud confirmed.

title: US Geological Survey reports $1 trillion in Afghan mineral wealth
note: $1 trillion mineral wealth estimate confirmed. Report was a Pentagon/USGS study.

title: US Navy SEALs kill Osama bin Laden in Abbottabad Pakistan
note: May 2, 2011 SEAL Team Six raid in Abbottabad confirmed.

title: NATO begins transferring security responsibility to Afghan forces
note: Transition process beginning July 2011 confirmed.

title: Quran burning at Bagram triggers nationwide riots killing dozens
note: February 2012 Bagram Quran burning riots confirmed; 30 total killed (not '30 killed US soldiers' — 4 Americans died). Event description is accurate.

title: Robert Bales massacre kills 16 Afghan civilians in Kandahar
note: March 11, 2012 Panjwai district massacre of 16 civilians by Staff Sgt. Bales confirmed.

title: Taliban open political office in Doha Qatar
note: Taliban Doha political office opened 2013 (not 2012 — opened June 2013). Year is off by one.

title: Afghan forces assume primary security responsibility nationwide
note: June 2013 formal handover of primary security responsibility confirmed.

title: Presidential election crisis resolved by US-brokered National Unity Government
note: Kerry-brokered NUG with Ghani as president and Abdullah as CEO confirmed.

title: NATO combat mission in Afghanistan formally ends
note: ISAF formally ended December 31, 2014, replaced by Resolute Support. Confirmed.

title: Bilateral Security Agreement signed allowing residual US forces
note: BSA signed by Ghani shortly after taking office in 2014. Confirmed.

title: Taliban briefly captures Kunduz city in northern Afghanistan
note: September-October 2015 Taliban capture of Kunduz confirmed; first major city since 2001.

title: Doctors Without Borders hospital bombed in Kunduz killing 42
note: October 3, 2015 MSF Kunduz Trauma Centre airstrike killing 42 confirmed.

title: Islamic State (ISIS-K) establishes presence in eastern Afghanistan
note: ISKP establishment in Nangarhar Province 2015 confirmed.

title: US kills Taliban leader Mullah Akhtar Mansour in drone strike in Pakistan
note: May 21, 2016 drone strike in Pakistani Balochistan killing Mansour confirmed.

title: Record 3.5 million Afghans internally displaced by conflict
note: 3.5M IDP figure for 2016 consistent with UN reporting.

title: Kabul suicide bombings kill hundreds in multiple mass casualty attacks
note: July 2016 Hazara protest bombing (80+ killed) confirmed; multiple mass-casualty attacks in 2016 Kabul confirmed.

title: Massive truck bomb in Kabul diplomatic quarter kills 150
note: May 31, 2017 truck bomb near German Embassy killing 150+ confirmed.

title: Taliban controls or contests 44% of Afghan territory
note: SIGAR reported Taliban controlled/contested ~44% of districts in 2017. Confirmed.

title: US-Taliban direct peace negotiations begin in Doha
note: Direct US-Taliban talks under Khalilzad began 2018 in Doha, sidelining Afghan government. Confirmed.

title: Record Afghan civilian casualties reported by UN
note: UNAMA 2018 annual report recorded highest-ever civilian casualties (10,000+ killed or wounded). Confirmed.

title: Presidential election produces disputed result between Ghani and Abdullah
note: September 2019 disputed election with both Ghani and Abdullah claiming victory confirmed.

title: US-Taliban Doha Agreement signed for phased withdrawal
note: February 29, 2020 Doha Agreement confirmed; 14-month withdrawal timeline confirmed.

title: Intra-Afghan peace talks open in Doha
note: September 12, 2020 intra-Afghan talks opening confirmed.

title: COVID-19 pandemic overwhelms Afghan health system
note: COVID-19 impact on Afghanistan's fragile health system in 2020 documented. WHO 10M infected estimate cited in description is plausible.

title: Biden administration announces complete US withdrawal
note: April 2021 Biden withdrawal announcement confirmed; later moved to August 31.

title: Taliban launches rapid military offensive capturing all provincial capitals
note: Taliban offensive beginning May 2021, capturing all provincial capitals. Confirmed.

title: Taliban captures Kabul and Afghan government collapses
note: August 15, 2021 Taliban takeover and Ghani fleeing confirmed.

title: Chaotic Kabul airport evacuation of 120,000 people
note: ~120,000 evacuated confirmed by US government figures.

title: ISIS-K suicide bombing at Kabul airport kills 170 including 13 US troops
note: August 26, 2021 Abbey Gate bombing confirmed; 169-182 Afghans + 13 US service members killed.

title: Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan re-established by Taliban
note: Taliban re-declared Islamic Emirate August 2021 under Haibatullah Akhundzada. Confirmed.

title: Taliban bans women from secondary education and most employment
note: Immediate Taliban bans on girls' secondary school and women's employment confirmed.

title: US freezes $9.5 billion in Afghan central bank reserves
note: ~$9.5B in Afghan central bank reserves frozen by US in August 2021 confirmed.

title: Catastrophic humanitarian crisis as 23 million face acute hunger
note: WFP 23M facing acute hunger figure for 2022 is cited in multiple reports.

title: Taliban bans women from universities completing total educational exclusion
note: December 2022 university ban confirmed.

title: Devastating earthquake kills 1,000 in Paktika and Khost provinces
note: June 22, 2022 5.9 magnitude earthquake; 1,036 confirmed killed. Accurate.

title: US kills al-Qaeda leader Ayman al-Zawahiri in Kabul drone strike
note: July 31, 2022 CIA drone strike killing Zawahiri on his Kabul balcony confirmed.

title: Afghan economy contracts by 20-30% since Taliban takeover
note: World Bank/IMF 20-30% GDP contraction estimates confirmed in multiple reports.

title: ISKP launches major attacks on Taliban military and Shia civilians
note: ISKP high-casualty attacks on Taliban and Hazara Shia mosques in 2022 confirmed.

title: Taliban bans women from working for NGOs and UN agencies
note: December 2022 NGO ban extended to UN April 2023. Confirmed.

title: Massive 6.3 magnitude earthquakes kill 1,400 in Herat Province
note: October 7, 2023 6.3 magnitude earthquake; death toll 1,400-2,400 depending on source. Confirmed.

title: UN Special Rapporteur accuses Taliban of gender apartheid
note: UN Special Rapporteur gender apartheid characterization confirmed.

title: Taliban resumes public executions and amputations
note: Taliban public executions and amputations resumed 2022-2023. Confirmed by HRW and UN reports.

title: Pakistan orders expulsion of 1.7 million Afghan refugees
note: October-November 2023 Pakistan expulsion of 1.7M undocumented Afghans confirmed.

title: Taliban enacts Law on Promotion of Virtue and Prevention of Vice
note: August 2024 morality law confirmed.

title: Catastrophic flooding kills hundreds across northern Afghanistan
note: May 2024 Baghlan and northern provinces flooding; 300+ killed confirmed.

title: ISKP conducts major attack on Moscow concert hall killing 145
note: March 22, 2024 Crocus City Hall attack; 149-151 killed. Description says 145 — slightly low but within initial reporting range. ISKP responsibility confirmed.

title: Pakistan-Afghanistan border tensions escalate over Durand Line
note: October 2025 border clashes confirmed as worst conflict since 2021 Taliban takeover; Taliban refusal to recognize Durand Line well-documented.

title: Taliban bans women from speaking in public and enforces full face veil
note: August 2024 morality law codified women's voice and face restrictions; enforcement escalated in 2025. Confirmed.

title: International Court of Justice case on Taliban gender apartheid advances
note: Canada, Germany, Australia, Netherlands brought CEDAW-based case to ICJ. Note: case uses CEDAW, not Genocide Convention as stated in description — minor factual inaccuracy in event description.
